title: refactor: Migrate handlers to rpc-spec (E)
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Migrates `deposit_authorized`, `nft_buy_offers` and `nft_sell_offers` onto `xrpl-rpc-spec` (bumped to 0.1.29), following the pattern of the earlier parts. Builds on #8573.

## Context of Change

- **`deposit_authorized`:** the spec now parses `source_account`, `destination_account` and `credentials`, and the hand-written checks are gone. The checks that read the ledger stay in the handler: accounts exist, credentials exist, are accepted, aren't expired, belong to the source, and aren't duplicated. Includes upstream's zero credential ID fix (#8533).
- **`nft_buy_offers` / `nft_sell_offers`:** both now derive from a shared `NFTOffersHandlerBase` (`NFTOffersCommon`), which replaces `NFTOffersHelpers.h`. The spec parses `nft_id`, `limit` and `marker`.
- **CMake:** `deposit_authorized` and `nft_offers_common` are added to the spec instantiations.

## API Impact

No change to successful responses. A request with a single problem returns the same error as before, with one exception:

- `nft_buy_offers` / `nft_sell_offers`: an `nft_id` that is an array or object now returns `invalidParams` instead of `internal`.

A request with more than one problem may now report a different one (`API-CHANGELOG.md`). An invalid `ledger_hash`/`ledger_index` is now reported first, an invalid `credentials` array or `marker` is reported before the ledger lookups, and a malformed `credentials` element is now reported before an earlier element that doesn't exist on the ledger.

title: chore: Simplify `account` and `ident` checks via rpc-spec
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Bumps `xrpl-rpc-spec` to 0.1.29 and simplifies the `account_info` and `account_lines` handlers to match. Handler `Input` types no longer wrap a `std::expected` in a `std::optional`.

## Context of Change

`account_info` used to carry `account` and `ident` as two `std::optional<DeferredAccountId>` members, and `account_lines` carried `peer` as one. Each handler had to check whether the field was present and then whether it decoded (`input.peer->has_value()`, `**input.peer`).

In 0.1.29, `AccountError` gains `Missing`:
- `account_info` has one `DeferredAccountId account`. The spec binds both `ident` and `account` to it, and a missing account is still rejected in the spec.
- `account_lines`' `peer` is a `DeferredAccountId` that defaults to `Missing`. An empty string also counts as `Missing`.

The handlers now check `has_value()` once. A malformed account is still reported by the handler, after the ledger is resolved and with the ledger fields in the response, as before.

No behaviour or wire-format change.

## API Impact

None.

title: feat: Add TransactionProposal invariants for Cosign
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Adds `ValidTransactionProposal`, a global invariant for the `TransactionProposal` ledger entry.

The invariant enforces two properties:

1. **Effect whitelist.** Only `TransactionProposalCreate` may create a proposal and only `SponsorshipTransfer` may modify one, with the exact counts the result allows. A proposal is deleted only by a successful `TransactionProposalCancel`, or together with the Ticket it is keyed to. A deleted Ticket takes its proposal along. A failed `TransactionProposalCreate`, `TransactionProposalCancel`, or `SponsorshipTransfer` must leave no trace.
2. **Canonical signer arrays.** Collected signer arrays stay sorted by account, free of duplicates, and within `STTx::kMaxMultiSigners` (32) and `kMaxBatchSigners` (24).

### Context of Change

This is the invariant layer for the On-Chain Cosigner work ([XLS-0103](https://github.com/shawnxie999/XRPL-Standards/blob/cosign/XLS-0103-onchain-cosigner/README.md)). Property 1 restates spec section 4.5; property 2 restates the signer-array rules in sections 4.2.2, 4.6 and 6.1.

It is a **global** invariant rather than part of `TransactionProposalCreate::visitInvariantEntry`. The properties are about the ledger entry and must hold whichever transactor touches it. `TransactionProposalCancel` and reserved-ticket cleanup are admitted explicitly.

Earlier revisions also reconciled every `OwnerCount` move exactly. They held a Create or Cancel to the one Ticket it pays with, and re-checked the Cancel's named proposal and its authorization. title: fix: Resolve amendment_enabled names through the feature registry
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

The `amendment_enabled` host function now resolves an amendment name with `getRegisteredFeature` (the compiled-in feature list) instead of `AmendmentTable::find`. Unknown names return 0. Whether the amendment is enabled still comes from the ledger's rules. The 32-byte id form is unchanged.

## Context of Change

`AmendmentTable` names are node-local. Two validators with the same ledger could therefore give a contract different answers for `amendment_enabled("X")` and compute different results for the same transaction.

The compiled-in feature list is the same on every node running the same binary, and a node whose binary does not know an enabled amendment is amendment-blocked, so all validating nodes agree.

## Test Plan

Added a case to `AmendmentTable_test`. A `[veto_amendments]` line gives TokenEscrow the misspelled name "TokenEscr", which renames it in the node's real AmendmentTable. The host function must still answer by the compiled-in name: "TokenEscrow" reads 1 (enabled on the ledger) and "TokenEscr" reads 0. Without the fix, both answers are reversed.

body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Migrates three account handlers, `account_info`, `account_lines` and `account_channels`, onto the shared `xrpl-rpc-spec` library (0.1.25), following #8561.

## Context of Change

Part of the rpc-spec migration; follows #8561.

- **Handlers:** each one becomes a class with `Input`/`Output`, `process()` and `writeResult()`, dispatched through `handle<XHandler>`. The spec now parses `account`/`ident`, `peer`, `destination_account`, `ignore_default`, `queue`, `limit` and `marker`, so the hand-written field checks are gone. `doAccountInfo`, `doAccountLines` and `doAccountChannels` are deleted.
- **`account_info`:** `ident` is read only when `account` is absent. A malformed account is still reported after the ledger lookup, with the ledger fields. The API v2 check that `signer_lists` is a bool stays in the handler, after the account is found, so its error still carries `account_data`.
- **`account_lines`:** a malformed `account` or `peer` is still reported after the ledger lookup, with the ledger fields. An empty `peer` still means no filter.
- **`account_channels`:** an empty `destination_account` still means no filter.
- **`limit` / `marker`:** handled as in #8561. The handler clamps `limit` for non-unlimited roles. `account_lines` and `account_channels` now use the shared `parseAccountMarker()`.
- **CMake:** the three handlers are added to `rpcspec_generate_instantiations`.
- **Tests:** error cases now check `error_code`. The API v2 non-bool `signer_lists` case in `AccountInfo_test` sent invalid JSON and never reached the handler; it now does.

## API Impact

No change to successful responses, or to any request with a single problem. A request with more than one problem may now report a different one (`API-CHANGELOG.md`):

- An invalid `ledger_hash`/`ledger_index` is reported before a missing or invalid `account` (or `ident`).
- An invalid `limit` or `marker`, or for `account_lines` a non-string `peer`, is reported before `lgrNotFound`

## High Level Overview of Change

`VaultWithdraw` now charges the issuer's transfer fee when a holder withdraws to a third party. Gated by `fixCleanup3_5_0`.

## Context of Change

Every vault withdrawal called `accountSend` with the transfer fee waived, so a deposit followed by a withdrawal to a third party moved IOUs and MPTs without paying the fee.

With the amendment enabled, the withdrawer's vault position pays the fee:

- A fixed-asset request delivers the requested amount and redeems enough shares to cover the gross cost.
- A fixed-share request burns the requested shares and delivers the amount left after the fee.
- Withdrawals to the submitter or to the issuer stay fee-free, and so do withdrawals submitted by the issuer.

title: fix: Add limits for the number of entries in the type, imports, and exports sections in a wasm module
body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Caps the number of entries in a wasm module's type, import and export sections, and the length of import and export names. The check runs before the module is compiled. A module that exceeds a cap is refused with a new `Limit` status, kept separate from ordinary malformed bytecode, so likely abuse can be told apart in the logs. Transaction results are unchanged: `temINVALID_BYTECODE` at preflight, `tecINTERNAL` at apply.

## Context of Change

`Module::new` parses, validates and stores every type, import and export entry. That work happens before a `Store` exists, so no fuel is charged for it. wasmi's `EnforcedLimits` has no setting for these sections. The only limits are wasmparser's hard-coded ones: 1,000,000 entries per section and 100,000 bytes per name. In testing, wasmi **accepted** a module declaring 1M types after 387 ms of uncharged work on every node that compiled it.

**Approach.** `compile` now runs `check_section_counts` before `Module::new`. Because `compile` is the only path to a `Module`, `check`, `check_all` and `run` all enforce the same caps. The scan:
- reads each section's entry count from its header, which costs almost nothing;
- reads names only after the section's count has passed its cap;
- stops at the code section, so function bodies and data are never read;
- skips anything that doesn't parse, so `Module::new` still reports malformed modules with wasmi's own messages.

**Caps** (new public constants in `xrpl-wasm-vm`):

| Constant | Value | Example contracts use |
|---|---|---|
| `MAX_TYPES` | 2048 | ≤ 9 |
| `MAX_IMPORTS` | 256 | ≤ 9 (the ABI has ~60 host functions) |
| `MAX_EXPORTS` | 256 | ≤ 5 |
| `MAX_NAME_BYTES` | 256 | ≤ 14 |

These values were chosen to leave far more room than any real contract needs, while staying low enough that reaching one signals a deliberately built module.

body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Migrates three account handlers, `account_currencies`, `account_nfts` and `account_offers`, onto the shared `xrpl-rpc-spec` library (0.1.23), following the pattern set in #8484.

## Context of Change

Part of the rpc-spec migration; follows #8484.

- **Handlers:** each one becomes a class with `Input`/`Output`, `process()` and `writeResult()`, dispatched through `handle<XHandler>`. The spec now parses `account`/`ident`, `limit` and `marker`, so the hand-written field checks are gone. `doAccountCurrencies`, `doAccountNFTs` and `doAccountOffers` are deleted.
- **`limit`:** the spec parses it, and the handler clamps it to the `tuning` range for non-unlimited roles, as `readLimitField` did.
- **`account_offers` marker:** the `index,hint` split moves into a local `parseMarker()`. The check that the marker's object belongs to the account stays in the handler.
- **`JsonFieldView::isNull()`:** required by spec 0.1.23's `NullAs` modifier.
- **CMake:** the three handlers are added to `rpcspec_generate_instantiations`.

## API Impact

No change to successful responses, or to any request with a single problem. A request with more than one problem may now report a different one (`API-CHANGELOG.md`):

- An invalid `ledger_hash`/`ledger_index` is reported before an invalid or missing `account`.
- An invalid `limit` or `marker` is reported before `lgrNotFound` or `actNotFound`.

title: feat: Add TransactionProposalCancel & Cosign Ticket reservation
body:
Implementation of https://github.com/XRPLF/XRPL-Standards/pull/613 (XLS-0103 On-Chain Cosigner). Follow-up to #8205, which introduced the `Cosign` amendment and `TransactionProposalCreate`.

## High Level Overview of Change

Adds `TransactionProposalCancel` (tx type 94, field `ProposalID`), the second transaction of the Cosign proposal lifecycle. It deletes a `TransactionProposal` ledger entry and releases the reserve held by its Owner or reserve sponsor.

While a proposal is live, only its Owner, the proposed transaction's `Account`, or the `Delegate` named in it may cancel it. Anyone else gets `tecNO_PERMISSION`. Once the proposal is terminal, anyone may delete it (XLS-0103 §7.2). A proposal is terminal when its `Expiration` has passed, or the ledger is strictly past the proposed transaction's `LastLedgerSequence`.

Introduces Ticket reservation (XLS-0103 §4.2.1). While a proposal keyed to a Ticket exists, only that proposal's own proposed transaction may consume the Ticket. Any other transaction spending it fails with the new retryable `terTICKET_RESERVED` code. This stops unrelated activity on the target account from invalidating a proposal while signatures are collected.

A reserved Ticket is consumed either by the proposed transaction executing or by `AccountDelete` sweeping the target's Tickets. Either way, the stale proposal is deleted automatically and its reserve released (XLS-0103 §4.5).

`TransactionProposalCreate` now also rejects proposing a `TransactionProposalCancel`. It likewise rejects a proposed `Batch` whose inner transactions include a proposal transaction, a pseudo-transaction, or a nested `Batch`.

body:
## High Level Overview of Change

Migrates the first two function handlers, `book_changes` and `transaction_entry`, onto the shared `xrpl-rpc-spec` library (0.1.21), and makes the spec's `::rpc::Status` xrpld's only RPC status type. This sets the pattern the remaining handlers will follow: a class with `Input`/`Output`, `process()` and `writeResult()`.

Part of the rpc-spec migration; follows #8345.

## Context of Change

- **One dispatch table (`Handler.cpp`):** `kClassHandlerArray`, `joinHandlers()` and `handlerFrom<>()` are gone. Every method is a row in `kHandlerArray`, which holds its name, role, condition, API range and command-line flag. A migrated handler differs only in `Method::of<&handle<XHandler>>()` instead of `Method::of<&byRef<&doX>>()`, so the static metadata on `LedgerHandler`/`VersionHandler` is removed.
- **`BookChangesHandler`:** the spec's ledger selector, then `computeBookChanges`.
- **`TransactionEntryHandler`:** `develop` checks `tx_hash` only after resolving the ledger, and reports it as a bare `error` beside the ledger fields. Spec 0.1.21 therefore leaves `tx_hash` to the handler on xrpld, and `process()` runs the checks in `develop`'s order.
- **`RPCLedgerHelpers`:** `injectLedgerFields()` is extracted from `lookupLedger`, for handlers that start their response from the ledger fields.
- **`Status`:** `src/xrpld/rpc/Status.h` and `detail/Status.cpp` are deleted. The ledger helpers, `Handler::Method`, `callMethod` and `doCommand` return `::rpc::Status`, which converts implicitly from `ErrorCodeI` since spec 0.1.21. Every `doCommand` caller already discarded the status.
- **Deleted:** `doBookChanges` and `doTransactionEntry`, and `Status_test.cpp`, which covered only helpers that are gone.
- **Spec 0.1.21:** `transaction_entry`'s `tx_hash` handling on xrpld; an implicit `Status(XrpldError)` and `Status::kOK`.
